trickyParts: Below 1280px styles.css forces every input and select to font-size 1rem (the iOS focus-zoom guard), so Tailwind text sizes cannot shrink the status and priority pills on a phone; the native priority select was 128px because of its 'Priority —' option plus the dropdown arrow. It is now appearance-none (text-only, like the status pill) with the unset label 'Priority', which leaves 14px of slack for Close on the 316px phone row even with this box's wide DejaVu Sans fallback font.

The details rail must be a real box to be a scroll container, so the xl:contents / 2xl:flex breakpoints are gone: the rail is min-w-0 flex-nowrap overflow-x-auto with flex-basis auto and NO grow, so on a shared row it takes only its content width (the flex-1 title keeps the free space) and alone on its line it shrinks to the line and scrolls. Round one shipped it with grow, which split the free space with the title below 1280 and squeezed a 41-character title to 61px at 1200 (main 168); the reviewer caught it. The state-actions box lost shrink-0 and gained min-w-0 so a long approval row wraps inside the card instead of overflowing it (approval.e2e.ts caught this).

The Playwright locator getByLabel('Route') matches the route button's aria-label 'Messages default to no route' as well as the input, so the button is not rendered while the route form is open; the form itself now renders under the header rows rather than inside the nowrap line.

Harness gotcha: packages/dispatch's unit suite (classes-in-build-css.test.ts) rebuilds web/dist WITHOUT VITE_DISPATCH_E2E=1. Running the e2e suite against that production build fails live.e2e.ts (two stream connections on load, a cold reconnect) — rebuild with the flag before any e2e run after bun test.

The whose-turn badge leads the details line at every width (one DOM position) instead of trailing it with ml-auto: at 1280 with the sidebar and margin open the line is 502px and cannot hold every detail, so a trailing badge would be scrolled out of view.

A React inline callback ref (ref={(node) => node?.focus()}) is re-invoked on every render, so using it to autofocus the route input re-stole focus from the title editor on each header re-render (issue-writes.test.tsx caught it). The route input is focused once by an effect keyed on routeEditing; the title input keeps the inline pattern because it is the only field that uses it.
